increment_paragraph: **OUT-SLOT-MEMBER-THEN-FRESH** (USER DECISION 2026-11-28: option (a), then on its stop (a1)+(b); gateway rule 96, rule 74l amended, contract spec C04.19.4.1; `QCore.MemberMoveOut`; [report](../../reports/out-slot-member-then-fresh/README.md)). The custody claim held: `rd_kafka_assignment`/`rd_kafka_subscription` move the op's `rko_u.assign.partitions`/`subscribe.topics` into the caller's slot and null it before `rd_kafka_op_destroy`, whose arm would free it. (a1): `resource_member_owned(result, TAG.PATH) when FIELD == VALUE` states an owned member of a result under its decided discriminant, admitted beside a nullable result (never with the liveness part); `rd_kafka_op_req2` declares its reply's discriminant (`type | RD_KAFKA_OP_REPLY`) and the two owned members (sync, `quirin-audit pin` at 66910c10 and 046accf6, locks in the commit; the edit registered in the SP2 checkpoint chain). Rule 96 (`legacy_member_move_out.rs`): a read `D = B->M;` the next statement nulls moves the member's object to `D`, an alias of a child the body linked alone or a fresh possibly-null site from an unspent owned-member state in a body that writes `M` only to null it; an object handed to a call spends its owned states, a store over an unspent owned member is refused, and everything else is the read's own lowering. Rule 74l mode (b): rule 85's null entry alone publishes a `null_only` summary, read only into a known-null slot; every other caller is refused by name, the callee's row keeps 74l (2), and an uncovered C04.13 class stays refused. Lean: 19 audited theorems, vectors bound to `MOVE_OUT_VECTORS` and `SLOT_MODE_VECTORS`. Fixtures show each positive reading (stated and linked move-outs released `Safe`, a known-null caller of a mode-(b) callee `Safe`, ignored deliveries leaking). The two rows stay `Unknown`: they bind the slot before `rd_kafka_op_destroy`, which rule 11r(8) reads as possibly writing caller memory, and no compiled caller passes a known-null slot. Opt-in `current --monkey-linked` over Fluent Bit 046accf6, each run on its own tree and binary: base 287dce8ed and tip b1cfce380 both 1,209/2/3,586/7, no row moved and no leaf changed (the rows' req2 call reads the unresolved `rkcg`, so no owned state applies there), against a `none` prediction; system slice not containing the rows, pinned routes not runnable on the host. Scoped gate (full mode, provider gate selected) at b1cfce380: fmt, probes, Lean (537 audits) and the provider gate (package build/verify, 182 provider tests passed, fmt, clippy) 0; clippy and the Rust suite 101 on one example's non-exhaustive match (fixed in fb5f6e2e3; workspace clippy then 0, run_test_binaries 10,424 passed, 0 failed), Python 1 on the stale report index (regenerated; 814 tests then 0).

ledger.why: Discharged by OUT-SLOT-MEMBER-THEN-FRESH under USER DECISION 2026-11-28 (a1)+(b): the owned member of a result (contract spec C04.19.4.1, resource_member_owned, admitted beside a nullable result), gateway rule 96's read-and-null move-out (crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_member_move_out.rs) and rule 74l's mode (b), a null_only keep-or-deliver summary read only into a known-null slot; Lean QCore.MemberMoveOut (19 audited theorems); rd_kafka_op_req2 declares its reply discriminant and owned members. Pinned in crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/op_constructor_declarations.rs. The two rows were re-measured on the opt-in route and stay Unknown at their named leaves: their bodies bind the slot before rd_kafka_op_destroy, which rule 11r(8) reads as possibly writing caller memory (registered as OUT-SLOT-CALL-WRITE-FRESH-OBJECT), and no compiled caller passes a known-null slot.

ledger.title: Rule 11r(8) poisons a bound out slot at a call handed a fresh object the frame owns
ledger.text: OUT-SLOT-MEMBER-THEN-FRESH found rdkafka_subscription.c rd_kafka_assignment and rd_kafka_subscription refused after rule 96 and mode (b): they store the moved member into *partitions/*topics before rd_kafka_op_destroy(rko), and rule 11r(8) (legacy_out_slot_call_write.rs) reads the local pointer rko as possibly designating caller memory, so the bound slot is poisoned and no summary validates (pin a_slot_bound_before_the_destroy_stays_refused). rko is a fresh owned object of the frame (rd_kafka_op_req2's result), but the callee may still reach caller memory through the object's own members. Their `!*out && !err` test and the indirect accesses (rkcg->rkcg_ops, rko->rko_err) block them besides. DISCHARGE: decide whether a call whose only reaching actual is a fresh owned object this frame acquired, released by the call, may spare a bound slot (with the premise on the object's members stated), with Lean parity in QCore.OutSlotCallWrite; re-measure the two rows.
